# Map and vendor provenance

This records only what the repository itself shows. The application imports `vendor/atlas-geo.js` and fetches `vendor/atlas-land-110m.json`; `vendor/atlas-LICENSES.txt` carries their licence texts.

Natural Earth terms: https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/

| Asset | Recorded source, scale and version | Recorded projection and licence | Not recorded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `route-land.svg` | README identifies the coastline as Natural Earth. No source scale or dataset version is recorded for this SVG. | SVG viewBox is `0 0 900 450`. The flat-map coordinate function `routes.js:mapPoint` is equirectangular: `[(lon + 180) * 2.5, (90 - lat) * 2.5]`; the SVG itself has no projection annotation. README and NOTICE identify Natural Earth land as public domain. | Generation script, exact input file/download URL, Natural Earth release, source scale, generation projection parameters, simplification and rounding procedure are not recorded. The filename does not establish a 1:110m source. |
| `route-land-detail.svg` | Embedded comment explicitly identifies Natural Earth 1:50m land. No dataset version is recorded. | Embedded comment states “Equirectangular projection” and “public domain”. SVG viewBox is `0 0 90000 45000`; README identifies the 1:50m layer as loaded on zoom. | Generation script, exact input file/download URL, Natural Earth release, full projection parameters, simplification and rounding procedure are not recorded. The `?v=1` loading suffix in map-viewport.js is not a recorded dataset release. |
| `vendor/atlas-land-110m.json` | `vendor/atlas-LICENSES.txt` states world-atlas 2.0.2 using Natural Earth public-domain data. Filename records 110m scale (1:110 million). | JSON is TopoJSON with a `land` object, geographic bbox and quantization transform. `atlas-globe.js` converts it with `feature` and displays it using `geoOrthographic().clipAngle(90).precision(0.65)`; orthographic is the runtime display projection. Natural Earth is public domain; the licence file also includes the world-atlas permission notice. | Natural Earth release, exact acquisition URL, extraction/generation script, original projection/CRS declaration, and procedure or command choosing quantization/rounding are not recorded. The numeric transform is present, but does not document that procedure. |
| `vendor/atlas-geo.js` | `vendor/atlas-LICENSES.txt` records bundled d3-geo 3.1.1, d3-array 3.2.5, internmap 2.0.3 and topojson-client 3.1.0. This is projection/conversion code; geographic source scale is not applicable. | Exports `feature`, `geoDistance`, `geoGraticule`, `geoOrthographic`, `geoPath`; the globe uses the orthographic projection above. The licence file gives d3-geo's ISC licence text, the MIT licence of GeographicLib (code included in d3-geo), and the licence notices for d3-array, internmap and topojson-client. | Bundle entry source, bundler name/version/command, dependency lockfile, build options, minification settings, and reproducible generation script are not recorded. No separate bundle version is recorded. |
